newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO - Former Court of Appeal Judge Simon Li announced his intention to run for the post of chief executive. Competition for the top post is now between two former judges and two businessmen.

-- China's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office has decided not to accept offers of entertainment from Hong Kong people before the future chief executive is selected and the provisional legislature is established at the end of the year, to avoid being accused of interfering with the selection process.
-- APPLE DAILY - The Hong Kong Jockey Club is investigating a suspected race-fixing scandal involving $100 million dollars.
-- WEN WEI PO - Police in Guangdong province held anti-illegal immigration excercises at the Hong Kong-Guangdong border yesterday.

-- Minister of Foreign Economic Relations and Trade Wu Yi urged the United States to take solid measures to help China join the World Trade Organisation and solve the issue of China's Most Favoured Nations status once for all.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES - Although Hopewell Holdings had announced it is selling Consolidated Electric Power Asia to Southern Co of the United States, a Southeast Asian consortium had lodged a new purchase proposal to Hopewell.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL - Fashion chain Joyce is considering opening a third "World of Joyce" boutique in South Korea.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - Two chief executive candidates, Tung Chee-hwa and Peter Woo, yesterday gave their backing to Chief Secretary Anson Chan and the entire civil service, urging them to stay on through the handover.

-- Top-level trade delegations from Hong Kong and the United States will meet in Washington in an effort to break an impasse in negotiations over alleged illegal trading practices by the territory's textile producers.
-- HONG KONG STANDARD - An American investment banker said that more than two dozen Taiwan companies were likely to list on U.S. stock exchanges in the next three years.
